Quezon City Ordinance SP-2868, Series of 2019: Total Ban on Distribution of Plastic Bags
Simulation summary based on public sources, not the full legal text.

Section 1. Distribution of plastic bags to customers is totally banned from the ordinance's effectivity.
Section 2. Covered sellers include shopping malls, supermarkets, department stores, grocery stores, fast-food chains, restaurants, drugstores and pharmacies, and, under a separate classification, market vendors and similar sellers.
Section 3. Brown (paper) bags are scheduled for a later phase of the ban. (This phase was deferred during the COVID-19 state of calamity by SP-3066, S-2021.)
Section 4. Certain retailers must submit annual reports, which are connected to their environmental clearance.
Section 5. The ordinance amends the city's Plastic Recovery System Fee and Green Fund rules (SP-2140, S-2012).

brief.summary: This ordinance prohibits the distribution of plastic bags by covered retailers in Quezon City.
brief.what_changes: Retailers must stop giving out plastic bags and begin using alternative packaging materials, complying with reporting requirements.
scenes: A customer leaves a supermarket with groceries still in plastic bags, noting the new rule.
A fast-food employee politely explains to a customer that plastic bags are no longer provided.
A market vendor adjusts his stall, offering reusable bags to customers instead of plastic.
A shopper brings their own reusable bag to a department store, bypassing the plastic bag option.
brief.where_when: Effective immediately, with brown paper bag implementation deferred due to the COVID-19 state of calamity.
brief.public_benefit: Reduced plastic waste and cleaner public spaces.
known_facts: Quezon City has ordinances banning discrimination based on SOGIESC.
RA 9003 (Ecological Solid Waste Management Act) requires waste segregation and prohibits littering.
issues: The definition of ‘retailer’ needs clarification for smaller businesses.
The cost of transitioning to alternative packaging materials is unclear.
A transition period for market vendors is needed, considering their specific circumstances.
Enforcement mechanisms and potential for abuse require further development.
The impact of the ban on low-income consumers needs to be addressed.

amendments.clause: Section 2, paragraph 1: ‘Covered retailers’ includes all delivery services operating within Quezon City, defined as any business providing goods or services to consumers via delivery.
amendments.change: Clarify ‘covered retailers’ to include all delivery services, ensuring broader applicability and addressing a key resident concern.
amendments.reason: Addresses concerns raised by 13 residents, including Mang Rudy, Kuya Jun, and Mr. Dizon.

amendments.clause: New Section: The Barangay shall provide subsidized brown paper bags to all market vendors and small retailers, with a maximum cost of PHP 5 per bag, for a period of six months following ordinance enactment.
amendments.change: Establishes a clear subsidy program for small businesses, directly responding to Aling Nena and Aling Tess’s requests.
amendments.reason: Resolves the concerns of 7 vendors and 2 store owners, including Aling Nena and Aling Tess.

amendments.clause: Section 4: The Barangay shall establish a transition period of one year for market vendors to adopt alternative packaging, with technical assistance and financial support provided.
amendments.change: Creates a defined transition period, acknowledging the unique needs of market vendors and facilitating a smoother shift.
amendments.reason: Addresses the specific concerns of 2 vendors and Aling Tess.
